citations.title: Design-based theory for causal inference from adaptive experiments
citations.locator: Appendix, subsection titled Lemmas for the central limit theorem, Lemma labeled \texttt{lem:martingale\_clt}

attestation.note: Transcribed from the primary arXiv source file Ada_0818_full.tex, lines 1684--1705, downloaded from export.arxiv.org on 2026-09-06. Notation macros were expanded without changing the mathematical statement.

env.world: A finite population of \(G\in2\mathbb N\) mutually isolated groups, each of common size \(n\in4\mathbb N\), observed at the endpoints of \(B\) two-period assignment blocks. Every unit \(i\in\mathcal I_n\) of every group \(g\in\mathcal G_G\) at every period \(t\le 2B\) carries a fixed schedule-indexed potential outcome \(Y_{gti}:\mathcal H_{2B}\to[-M,M]\) on the within-group treatment-and-saturation history space \(\mathcal H_{2B}=(\mathcal D\times\mathcal Q)^{2B}\), with \(\mathcal D=\{0,1\}\) and \(\mathcal Q=\{q_L,q_H\}=\{1/4,3/4\}\); \(\mathcal H_t\) is the corresponding history space through period \(t\). Under ordinary nonanticipation together with the imposed lag-one finite-memory restriction, the block endpoint of a two-period block whose exposure is held at \((d,q)\) is the sustained-exposure endpoint \(Y_{gbi}(d,q)\in[-M,M]\). The potential outcomes are fixed: the only randomness is the experimenter's two-stage assignment, and \(\mathcal F_b\) is generated by assignments and observed endpoints through block \(b\). Each group carries a prespecified centered baseline score \(H_g\) with \(|H_g|\le K_H\) and \(\sum_g H_g=0\); observed block-endpoint group means \(\bar Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{gb}\) and their grand mean \(\bar Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_b\) feed the predictable balance score \(V_{gb}\) with loading \(\lambda\), whose complete-randomization imbalance variance \(\sigma_b^2\) is confined to a window \([c_\sigma,C_\sigma]\). Growth of \(G\) relative to \(B\) is otherwise unconstrained between \(c_\rho\) and \(C_\rho\). The structural class \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) collects the arrays satisfying these conditions, and \(\mathcal W^{AB}\subseteq\mathcal M_{G,B}\) is the explicit alternating-block witness family.
env.notes: Search trace: `npm run search -- "finite population fixed potential outcomes randomization design" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search FiniteDesign / toMeasure / prodDesign`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{DesignCore,PotentialOutcome,Exposure,FiniteDesignMeasure,Product,TwoStage}.lean and Causalean/Experimentation/{TwoStageInterference,UnknownInterference,ExposureMappingInterference}/. Result: `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign` (DesignCore.lean) is EXACTLY this world's probability layer -- a pmf on a finite assignment space with `E`/`Var`/`Cov`/`ind`/`Pr` finite-sum algebra (`Cov_linear_comb`, `Var_linear_comb`, `E_sum`) and the measure bridge `FiniteDesign.toMeasure` (`FiniteDesignMeasure.lean`) for the asymptotic statements. REUSED, not rebuilt. The fixed schedule-indexed outcome family `Y_{gti} : H_{2B} -> [-M,M]`, the two-period-block sustained-exposure reduction `Y_{gbi}(d,q)`, the predictable balance score `V_{gb}`, and the class carrier are define-local (a history-indexed 2B-period schedule with lag-one memory has no Causalean analogue: `PotentialOutcome.ProperlySpecified` is single-period exposure factorization, a PARTIAL fit only). Analogous module for the schedule layer: Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/{Basic,Stratified}.lean (`WAssign`, `stratExpo`, `exists_strat_factor`) -- adapt from a single-period within-group exposure to the 2B-period history with the lag-one collapse. `c_\rho`/`C_\rho` are declared relative-growth constants that the delivered results deliberately do NOT constrain (the note's headline is that no restriction on G/B is needed); they are bound here as inert design constants and must not be smuggled into any theorem hypothesis. `\mathcal M_{G,B}` is realized as the `def:model-class` structure and is the ambient carrier every class-scoped statement quantifies over; `\mathcal W^{AB}` is the `def:adaptive-witness` construction.

env.world: At each block \(b\), conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), the first stage draws a balanced saturation sign vector \(x_b\) from the support \(\mathcal X_G=\{x\in\{-1,1\}^G:\sum_gx_g=0\}\). The uniform balanced-sign reference law is \(P_0(x)=\binom{G}{G/2}^{-1}\); the raw balance statistic \(Z_b(x)=G^{-1/2}\sum_gx_gV_{gb}\) is exactly standardized to \(W_b(x)=Z_b(x)/\sigma_b\), so \(\operatorname{Var}_0\{W_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}\}=1\). The soft radial weight \(f_{\eta,\kappa}(w)=\eta+(1-\eta)e^{-\kappa w^2}\in[\eta,1]\) with floor \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and curvature \(\kappa>0\) tilts \(P_0\) into the predictable soft-rerandomization law \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=P_0(x)f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b(x)\}/C_b\), normalized by \(C_b=\mathbb E_0[f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b\}\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}]\in[\eta,1]\). The realized sign fixes the group saturation \(Q_{gb}=q_H\) if \(x_{gb}=1\) and \(q_L\) otherwise. Conditionally on \(x_b\), the second stage draws exactly \(nQ_{gb}\) treated units uniformly without replacement in each group, independently across groups, and holds both stages fixed across the two periods of the block. The within-group exposure probability is \(p_{1q}=q\), \(p_{0q}=1-q\); \(I_{gbi,dq}\) indicates the realized exposure cell, whose conditional first- and second-order inclusion probabilities \(\pi_{gbi,dq}\) and \(\pi_{k\ell,b}\) are known and logged by the randomizer.
env.notes: Search trace: `npm run search -- "two-stage compound design conditional within-group randomization" --cluster experimentation`, `npm run search -- "complete randomization inclusion probability pair"`, `lean_local_search compound / prodDesign / completeRandomization_incl / completeRandomization_incl_pair / tilt / reweight`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{TwoStage,Product,ProductVariance,CompoundVariance,Designs/CompleteRandomization,Designs/Stratified,Exposure}.lean and Causalean/Experimentation/Sequential/AdaptiveDesign.lean. FOUND and REUSED: (i) `compound D1 D2 : FiniteDesign (Omega1 x (forall i, alpha i))` is exactly the block's stage-1-then-independent-within-group structure, with the tower `E_compound_tower`, the total-variance law `Var_compound_eq_tower`, the stage-2 collapse `E_compound_factor`, and `Var_prod_linear_comb`; (ii) `completeRandomization n1 hn : FiniteDesign {S : Finset V // S.card = n1}` IS the uniform fixed-count law -- instantiated at `V = G-groups, n1 = G/2` it IS `P_0` on the balanced-sign support, and at `V = I_n, n1 = n*q` it IS the fixed-count second stage, with the first- and second-order inclusion probabilities already proved as `completeRandomization_incl` and `completeRandomization_incl_pair` (these directly supply `p_dq` and the within-group entries of `pi_{kl,b}` used by lem:pair-probability-control and thm:studentizer). NOT FOUND, hence define-local (small, build-inline): a soft-tilt combinator `softTilt D f : FiniteDesign Omega` with `p x = D.p x * f x / D.E f` -- `lean_local_search tilt / reweight` returned nothing in Causalean, and `lean_loogle`/`lean_leansearch` for a Mathlib pmf reweighting turned up only `PMF`-level `Measure.withDensity`, which is the wrong (measure-theoretic, un-normalized) abstraction for this finite-sum layer. Also NOT FOUND: a predictable chain of finite designs across B blocks -- `Causalean/Experimentation/Sequential/AdaptiveDesign.lean` (`AdaptiveExperiment`, `HasOverlap`, `propensity_pos_of_overlap`) is measure-theoretic over a Mathlib `Filtration`, a different abstraction from this finite-sum design layer; the B-block predictable chain is define-local, built by iterating `compound` over the block prefix so that `F_{b-1}` is realized as the realized path prefix (the same conditioning idiom Causalean's TwoStageInterference uses). Recorded as bypass-justified for `AdaptiveDesign.lean` only: the artifact is a purely finite, algebraic randomization layer, while that module is the measure-theoretic superpopulation flavor. The soft tilt and complement symmetry live in Helpers/SoftTilt.lean; the balanced-sign uniform-perfect-matching representation lives in Helpers/PerfectMatching.lean.

env.world: The causal target and its estimator live on the four exposure cells \((d,q)\in\mathcal D\times\mathcal Q\) with the fixed direct-and-spillover contrast coefficients \(c_{0q_L}=(-1/2,-1/2)^\top\), \(c_{1q_L}=(1/2,-1/2)^\top\), \(c_{0q_H}=(-1/2,1/2)^\top\), \(c_{1q_H}=(1/2,1/2)^\top\). The finite-population sustained-exposure means are \(\mu_{dq}\); the block target is \(\tau_b\in\mathbb R^2\) and the estimand is \(\tau=(\tau_D,\tau_S)^\top=B^{-1}\sum_b\tau_b=\sum_{d,q}c_{dq}\mu_{dq}\). The logged-probability Horvitz--Thompson estimators are \(\widehat\mu_{dq}\), the block vector \(\widehat\tau_b\), and the headline \(\widehat\tau=B^{-1}\sum_b\widehat\tau_b\). Within a group the saturation-specific causal score is \(m_{gbq}\), its Horvitz--Thompson counterpart \(\widehat m_{gbq}\), the centered sampling error \(e_{gbq}=\widehat m_{gbq}-m_{gbq}\) with conditional covariance \(T_{gbq}\), and the high-versus-low score difference \(a_{gb}=m_{gbq_H}-m_{gbq_L}\). The normalized block error \(R_b=\sqrt G(\widehat\tau_b-\tau_b)\) splits into the balanced-sign component \(A_b=G^{-1/2}\sum_gx_{gb}a_{gb}\) and the within-group component \(U_b=2G^{-1/2}\sum_ge_{gb,Q_{gb}}\), with covariance pieces \(K_b\), the complete-randomization benchmark \(\Sigma_{b,0}\), the soft-rerandomization covariance \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\), and the score-on-imbalance projection loading \(\beta_b\).
env.notes: Search trace: `npm run search -- "Horvitz Thompson estimator inverse probability weighted exposure mean unbiased" --cluster experimentation`, `npm run search -- "two-stage direct spillover effect estimator"`, `lean_local_search E_htTotal / htMean / muTrue / Cov_linear_comb`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/HT/{Estimator,Unbiased,Variance}.lean, Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/{Unbiased,Effects,Variance,BetweenGroupEffect}.lean, Causalean/Experimentation/ExposureMappingInterference/. Result: PARTIAL fits only, so define-local. `htTotal`/`htMean`/`htEffect` and `E_htTotal`/`E_htMean`/`E_htEffect` (HT/Estimator.lean, HT/Unbiased.lean) are the scalar, single-period, static-propensity HT layer; the artifact's estimator is R^2-valued over four exposure cells with a triple (block, group, unit) index and PREDICTABLE (history-dependent) inclusion probabilities, so the conclusion does not type-match and this is not a discharge. ANALOGOUS MODULES to adapt (recorded for F3): Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/HT/Unbiased.lean `E_htTotal` for the indicator-forced substitution `I*Yobs = I*y` then division by pi (the technique behind prop:exact-unbiasedness, needing only the extra conditional-on-F_{b-1} layer supplied by `E_compound_factor`); Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/HT/Variance.lean `Var_htTotal_cov` for the double-sum-of-covariances form of the block covariance (equation (8) of thm:studentizer); Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/BetweenGroupEffect.lean `Var_estDirect` for the two-stage between/within split of an EFFECT estimator. The vector-valued (R^2) lifting is the gap F3 must bridge -- `FiniteDesign.Cov_linear_comb`/`Var_linear_comb` (DesignCore.lean) are scalar and get applied coordinatewise. Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "Horvitz-Thompson design-based estimator"` / `lean_loogle "inclusion probability"`: nothing; Mathlib has no design-based survey-sampling layer.

env.world: The Gaussian comparison objects are the centered pairs \((A_b^\star,W_b^\star)\in\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R\) and \((R_b^\star,W_b^\star)\), each carrying the exact conditional \(P_0\)-covariance of its discrete counterpart and supported on that covariance range when the covariance is singular. The history-uniform transport modulus is a deterministic sequence \(\varepsilon_G\downarrow0\). The standard-normal soft-tilt shrinkage constant is \(v_{\eta,\kappa}=\{\eta+(1-\eta)(1+2\kappa)^{-3/2}\}/\{\eta+(1-\eta)(1+2\kappa)^{-1/2}\}\in(0,1)\). The limiting covariances are \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\) (soft rerandomization), \(\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}\) (complete randomization), and the precision-gain matrix \(P\), the deterministic limit of \(B^{-1}\sum_b\beta_b\beta_b^\top\).
env.notes: Search trace: `lean_local_search stdGaussian / multivariateGaussian / posSqrt / lambda1`, `lean_leansearch "centered Gaussian measure with given covariance on a finite dimensional space"`, `lean_loogle "Matrix.PosSemidef"`; scanned Causalean/Mathlib/{StandardGaussian,OperatorSqrt}.lean, Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/{TwoByTwoSpectralRoots,SingularValueWeyl}.lean, Causalean/Stat/CLT/{ChiSquared,GaussianLimit,MultivariateCLT}.lean, Mathlib/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/Multivariate.lean. REUSED: `Causalean.Mathlib.stdGaussian` (a mean-zero Gaussian on any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with `covarianceBilin_stdGaussian`, `isGaussian_stdGaussian`, `stdGaussian_mean`) plus `LinearMap.IsPositive.posSqrt`/`posSqrtCLM` (`posSqrt_mul_self`, `posSqrt_isPositive`) to realize the covariance-matched pair as `Sigma^{1/2} Z` -- this is exactly the singular-support construction the proof needs (the PSD square root exists without any positive-definiteness), so no eigenvalue lower bound is ever taken. `ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian` (Mathlib) supplies the N_2(0, Omega_RR) limit law object. `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.lambda1`/`lambda2`/`rootDiscriminant`/`lambda1_mul_lambda2`/`eigenvalue_eq_lambda1_or_lambda2` give the explicit ordered 2x2 spectrum used for lambda_min(Omega_RR) > 0 and det(P) > 0. Define-local (build-inline, small): `epsilon_G` as a deterministic modulus, `v_{eta,kappa}` as a closed-form scalar, and the covariance-range support predicate.

env.world: The observable studentizer is indexed by the block exposure-cell set \(\mathcal K_b=\mathcal G_G\times\mathcal I_n\times\mathcal D\times\mathcal Q\), whose element \(k=(g,i,d,q)\) carries the vector-valued outcome \(u_{k,b}=c_{dq}Y_{gbi}(d,q)\in\mathbb R^2\). The unordered impossible-pair set is \(\mathcal Z_b=\{\{k,\ell\}:k\ne\ell,\ \pi_{k\ell,b}=0\}\). The block estimator \(\widehat\Gamma_b\in\mathbb S^2\) is the pairwise Horvitz--Thompson covariance sum over the feasible pairs augmented by a diagonal Young completion over \(\mathcal Z_b\), whose deterministic excess is the positive-semidefinite completion bias \(D_b=(Gn^2)^{-1}\sum_{\{k,\ell\}\in\mathcal Z_b}(u_{k,b}+u_{\ell,b})(u_{k,b}+u_{\ell,b})^\top\). Averaging gives \(\widehat\Gamma=B^{-1}\sum_b\widehat\Gamma_b\), and clipping its two eigenvalues at the deterministic sequence \(r_B\downarrow0\) gives the invertible \(\widehat\Gamma_+\in\mathbb S_{++}^2\). At nominal noncoverage \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) the simultaneous Wald ellipse is \(\mathcal C_\alpha=\{t\in\mathbb R^2:GB(\widehat\tau-t)^\top\widehat\Gamma_+^{-1}(\widehat\tau-t)\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\}\).
env.notes: Search trace: `npm run search -- "conservative variance estimator zero joint probability Young completion" --cluster experimentation`, `npm run search -- "spectral clipping eigenvalue floor two by two symmetric matrix"`, `lean_local_search htA2 / E_htVarEst_add_htA2_ge / lambda1 / chiSqDist`, `lean_leansearch "chi squared distribution quantile continuity point"`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/ExposureMappingInterference/Variance/Conservative.lean, .../Asymptotics/{VarEstQuadBound,VarEstConsistencyConditions}.lean, Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/{TwoByTwoSpectralRoots,TwoByTwoSpectralProjector,SingularValueWeyl}.lean, Causalean/Stat/CLT/{ChiSquared,ChiSquaredProjection}.lean. REUSED: `Causalean.Stat.chiSqDist` with `stdGaussian_map_normSq` (the chi-squared law IS the pushforward of the squared standard-Gaussian norm) and `noAtoms_chiSqDist` (no atom at the positive quantile -- exactly the continuity point thm:wald-coverage needs at equation (22)); `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.lambda1`/`lambda2`/`rootDiscriminant_nonneg`/`lambda2_le_lambda1`/`lambda1_add_lambda2`/`lambda1_mul_lambda2`/`eigenvalue_eq_lambda1_or_lambda2` (TwoByTwoSpectralRoots.lean) give the explicit ordered 2x2 eigenvalues in closed quadratic form, which turns the spectral clipping at r_B and the Weyl-type step (15) of thm:studentizer into elementary algebra on the trace and discriminant rather than a general spectral-theorem argument; `topProjector`/`topProjector_isOrthogonalProjectorOntoTop` (TwoByTwoSpectralProjector.lean) gives the choice-free eigenprojector so the clipped matrix is defined without an arbitrary eigenvector sign. Define-local because Causalean's Young-completed estimator is scalar and static: `htA2` / `E_htVarEst_add_htA2_ge` / `htCovEstA` / `E_htEffectVarEstA_ge` (ExposureMappingInterference/Variance/Conservative.lean) is the SAME Young-inequality-on-the-zero-joint-pairs technique and is the ANALOGOUS MODULE F3 should adapt; the gap to bridge is (a) scalar -> 2x2 symmetric matrix conservativeness in Loewner order, (b) fixed -> predictable logged pair probabilities. Mathlib-side check `lean_loogle "Matrix.PosSemidef"` / `lean_leansearch "Loewner order inversion reverses"`: `Matrix.PosSemidef` and `Matrix.PosSemidef.det_nonneg` exist and cover the PSD algebra; the Loewner-inversion-reversal step (20) has no direct Mathlib lemma and is a small build-inline fact at 2x2 via the explicit roots.

ass:design-based-finiteness.notes: Modeling assumption (randomization stance): conditional on the fixed finite population, the only randomness is x_b and A_{gbi}. Kept as a threaded Prop -- never discharged, never escalated. Search trace: `npm run search -- "design based finite population fixed potential outcomes only randomness assignment" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search FiniteDesign / ProperlySpecified`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{DesignCore,PotentialOutcome}.lean. Result: in Causalean this stance is STRUCTURAL (a `FiniteDesign` is a pmf on the assignment space and potential outcomes are plain functions), so there is no named Prop to reuse; here the author atomizes it as its own `ass:` node, so it is encoded as one named Prop def asserting that the observed endpoint factors through the assignment via the fixed schedule. Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "randomization inference finite population"`: nothing (Mathlib has no design-based layer).

ass:partial-interference.notes: Modeling assumption (causal-structural, Hudgens-Halloran): Y_{gti} is invariant to assignments outside group g. Threaded, never discharged. Search trace: `npm run search -- "partial interference across groups invariance outside group" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search prodDesign / Cov_prod_disjoint_zero / y_eq_of_agree_on_interferers`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/{Basic,Stratified}.lean, Causalean/Experimentation/UnknownInterference/Basic.lean, Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{Product,ProductBlock}.lean. Result: PARTIAL fit, so define-local. In Causalean's TwoStageInterference partial interference is made STRUCTURAL by the product design (`prodDesign` over groups), not stated as a Prop; `UnknownInterference.y_eq_of_agree_on_interferers` is the closest named Prop but is about an arbitrary interference indicator on a Bernoulli design, and its conclusion does not type-match a 2B-period history-indexed schedule. ANALOGOUS: reuse `prodDesign` + `FiniteDesign.Cov_prod_apply_of_ne` / `Cov_prod_disjoint_zero` (Product.lean, ProductBlock.lean) as the machinery that turns this assumption into the cross-group independence used by lem:score-decomposition.

ass:stratified-interference.notes: Modeling assumption (causal-structural): within group g the endpoint depends on the contemporaneous within-group assignment vector only through own treatment d and realized saturation q. Threaded, never discharged. Search trace: `npm run search -- "stratified interference own treatment number treated exposure factorization" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search ProperlySpecified / StratifiedInterference / stratExpo / exists_strat_factor`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{PotentialOutcome,Exposure}.lean and Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/Stratified.lean. Result: PARTIAL fit -- `DesignBased.ProperlySpecified` (`forall i z, yr i z = y i (expo i z)`) is the general exposure-factorization Prop and `TwoStageInterference.StratifiedInterference` is the Hudgens-Halloran count-of-others version; NEITHER type-matches, because this note's exposure is (own treatment, group SATURATION) on a 2B-period history-indexed schedule rather than a single-period count. A partial fit is not a discharge, so this is define-local; F2 should nonetheless SHAPE it as an instance of the `ProperlySpecified` idiom with exposure map `h |-> (d_t, q_t)` so the downstream indicator-forced substitution lemmas (`expoInd_mul_Yobs`, `Yobs_eq_sum`) transfer by analogy.

ass:nonanticipation.notes: Modeling assumption (Bojinov-Rambachan-Shephard nonanticipation): histories agreeing through period t give the same period-t endpoint. Threaded, never discharged. Search trace: `npm run search -- "nonanticipating potential outcomes panel dynamic finite population" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search Nonanticipat / adapted / Predictable`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/{Sequential/AdaptiveDesign,DesignBased/PotentialOutcome}.lean and Causalean/Panel/. Result: ABSENT from Causalean -- the design-based layer has no dynamic/panel potential-outcome schedule at all, and `Sequential/AdaptiveDesign.lean` carries adaptivity of the DESIGN (`AdaptiveExperiment` over a Mathlib `Filtration`), not nonanticipation of the OUTCOME. Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "nonanticipating potential outcome"` / `lean_loogle "MeasureTheory.Adapted"`: `MeasureTheory.Adapted`/`IsPredictable` exist but are measure-theoretic process notions, the wrong abstraction for a deterministic invariance property of a fixed schedule. Build-inline as a prefix-agreement invariance Prop on `H_{2B}` (small).

ass:finite-memory-lag-one.notes: Modeling assumption, flagged NOVEL by the core (an imposed finite-memory restriction, not a consequence of ordinary nonanticipation): histories agreeing at periods t-1 and t give the same period-t endpoint. Threaded, never discharged; this and ass:nonanticipation together are what collapse the schedule to the sustained-exposure endpoint Y_{gbi}(d,q) used everywhere downstream. Search trace: `npm run search -- "finite memory lag one carryover potential outcome restriction" --cluster experimentation`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/ (all of DesignBased, TwoStageInterference, UnknownInterference, Sequential) and Causalean/Panel/AdoptionPath.lean. Result: ABSENT -- Causalean has no carryover/finite-memory layer. Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "finite memory dependence on last two coordinates"`: nothing relevant. Build-inline (small, a two-coordinate agreement invariance).

ass:imbalance-variance-window.notes: Modeling / design-regularity assumption: uniformly over blocks and realized histories, c_sigma <= sigma_b^2 <= C_sigma. This is a restriction on the realized design statistic (it is what makes the exact standardization W_b = Z_b/sigma_b legitimate and bounds |V_{gb}|/sigma_b in the perfect-matching envelope), NOT a general mathematical theorem -- so it stays a threaded hypothesis and is neither discharged nor escalated. Search trace: `npm run search -- "nondegenerate finite population variance lower bound uniform over history" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search SmuVar / Var_srs_mean / S1 / Stau`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/{StageOne,Variance}.lean and Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/DesignCore.lean. Result: `SmuVar` and the Neyman sample variances `S1`/`S0`/`Stau` are the (n-1)-denominator population-variance DEFINITIONS this reuses in shape, but no library lemma asserts a two-sided window -- correctly so, since it is the author's assumption. Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "sample variance bounded below"`: nothing (it is a hypothesis, not a theorem).

ass:rr-covariance-stabilization.notes: Modeling assumption (predictable quadratic-variation stabilization): B^{-1} sum_b Sigma_{b,RR} ->_P Omega_RR. This is the note's deliberately SEPARATED covariance-limit condition -- the tldr and honest_scope both stress that the structural class does not imply it -- so it is a threaded hypothesis of thm:joint-design-clt / thm:studentizer / thm:wald-coverage / thm:projection-covariance and is neither discharged nor escalated. Search trace: `npm run search -- "predictable quadratic variation stabilization convergence in probability design" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search TendstoInProb / tendstoInProb_of_var / BoundedInProb`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/InProb.lean and Causalean/Stat/Limit/. REUSED for the ENCODING (not a discharge): `FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb` (InProb.lean) is the right convergence-in-probability predicate for this finite-design layer, with `.sub`/`.add`/`.abs`/`.const_mul` closure and `tendstoInProb_of_var` as the Chebyshev engine; the matrix-valued version is coordinatewise and build-inline. Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "convergence in probability of a sequence of random matrices"`: `MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure` exists but is the measure-theoretic sibling; the finite-design predicate is the matching abstraction.

ass:rr-limit-positive.notes: Modeling / regularity assumption: lambda_min(Omega_RR) > 0. Threaded (into thm:joint-design-clt, thm:studentizer, thm:wald-coverage), never discharged -- thm:projection-covariance deliberately does NOT use it, and that separation must be preserved. Search trace: `npm run search -- "positive definite limiting covariance minimum eigenvalue"` + `lean_local_search lambda1 / lambda2 / PosDef`; scanned Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/TwoByTwoSpectralRoots.lean and Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean. REUSED for the encoding: `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.lambda2` is the explicit smaller root of a 2x2 matrix, so `0 < lambda2 Omega_RR` is the closed-form statement of positive definiteness at this dimension (with `lambda2_le_lambda1`, `lambda1_mul_lambda2`, `eigenvalue_eq_lambda1_or_lambda2` linking it to `Matrix.PosDef`). Mathlib-side check `lean_loogle "Matrix.PosDef"`: `Matrix.PosDef` exists and is the alternative encoding; the explicit-root form is preferred because the whole studentizer chain is 2x2 and closed-form.

ass:cr-covariance-stabilization.notes: Modeling assumption: B^{-1} sum_b Sigma_{b,0} ->_P Omega_CR. Threaded into thm:projection-covariance only. Search trace: identical to [ass:rr-covariance-stabilization] (`npm run search -- "finite population covariance stabilization complete randomization limit"`, scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/InProb.lean and Causalean/Stat/Limit/); same result -- `FiniteDesign.TendstoInProb` supplies the predicate, nothing supplies the limit, correctly so since it is a hypothesis. Encoded exactly parallel to the RR version so the note's deliberate scope separation between the two stabilizations stays visible in the signatures.

ass:projection-stabilization.notes: Modeling assumption, flagged NOVEL by the core (an imposed predictable-array stabilization for the history-adaptive sequence, not attributable to Li-Ding-Rubin 2018): B^{-1} sum_b beta_b beta_b^T ->_P P. Threaded into thm:projection-covariance only; it is also what makes P >= 0 derivable inside that proof (a limit in probability of nonnegative quadratic forms), so it must NOT be strengthened to an assumed PSD hypothesis. def:adaptive-witness.notes: The explicit alternating-block family: for G in 4N, each sign pair (H_g, J_g) in {-1,1}^2 equally represented, lambda = 1, type-A blocks (a_Dg, a_Sg) = (H_g, J_g) with L = 0 and type-B blocks (a_Dg, a_Sg) = (J_g, H_g) with L = 4, theta_g = 4 a_Dg, delta_g = L - theta_g, h_g = a_Sg/2 + a_Dg - L/2, Y_{gbi}(d,q) = h_g + d(delta_g + theta_g q). thm:projection-covariance.notes: As G -> infinity, uniformly over blocks and histories, Sigma_{b,RR} = Sigma_{b,0} - (1 - v) beta_b beta_b^T + o(1); on sequences with the three stabilizations, Omega_RR = Omega_CR - (1 - v) P; and for fixed c != 0, strict variance improvement iff c^T P c > 0. Build-inline (in scope), no new substrate. Scope discipline to preserve: this theorem must NOT take ass:rr-limit-positive (the note is explicit that no positive-definiteness condition is used), and P >= 0 must be DERIVED as a limit in probability of nonnegative quadratic forms, not assumed. REUSED: `LinearMap.IsPositive.posSqrt` for the singular-covariance Gaussian construction (equation (4): E* = R* - beta W* with zero cross-covariance, hence independent by factorization of the joint characteristic function -- no inverse of the possibly singular score covariance is ever taken), `Causalean.Mathlib.covarianceBilin_stdGaussian`, and `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.lambda2` for the strict-positivity reading of the criterion. The Gaussian moment identities behind v_{eta,kappa} are built in [def:projection-gain]. STRUCTURAL NOTE for F2: this theorem's depends_on does not list def:model-class, but it invokes thm:weighted-gaussian-transport, which does; the class instance is supplied by the ambient S1 world binder rather than by minting an extra hypothesis, so P4 stays satisfied and no assumption is smuggled in.

prop:complete-randomization-reduction.notes: The boundary sanity reduction: at eta = 1 or kappa = 0 the weight is identically one, so P_RR = P_0, v = 1, Omega_RR = Omega_CR, and both tauhat and Gammahat collapse to the ordinary balanced two-stage HT constructions. No assumptions in depends_on, hence no hyps. Build-inline (in scope) and the cheapest node in the plan: `softTilt D 1 = D` is definitional once the normalizer is computed, and the rest is substitution plus the balanced-sign covariance identity Cov_0(x_g, x_h) = -1/(G-1), which `completeRandomization_incl_pair` supplies directly. F2 note: the statement must say the two PARAMETER RESTRICTIONS are equivalent AS RESTRICTIONS ON THE KERNEL, not that eta = 1 and kappa = 0 are equal -- the proof text is explicit about this and a careless encoding would assert a false equality.

prop:adaptive-full-rank-witness.notes: W^{AB} is in M_{G,B}, its type-A and type-B imbalance variances converge to 53/16 and 29/16, and P = (1/2){(1/53)[[36,6],[6,1]] + (1/29)[[4,10],[10,25]]} is positive definite with det P = 196/1537. No hyps: the proposition PROVES class membership and DERIVES all three stabilizations plus positive definiteness for the witness rather than assuming them -- F2 must not add a stabilization hypothesis here, since deriving them is the whole point of the node (and the reason lem:adaptive-witness-pre-membership-transport exists, to break the logical cycle with the class-level transport theorem). thm:weighted-gaussian-transport.notes: The technical engine: a deterministic epsilon_G -> 0 with the scalar, the A_b-quadratic and the R_b-quadratic soft-weighted moment comparisons all bounded by epsilon_G uniformly over blocks, histories and members of M_{G,B}, valid on the exact covariance range including when it is singular. hyps = [def:model-class], which BUNDLES ass:design-based-finiteness and ass:imbalance-variance-window (both in depends_on, both class members), so P4 is satisfied without listing them twice. PAPER-OWNED and IN SCOPE (defer_tier false, gate false) even though it is the hardest node: it is the note's own contribution, so proof difficulty may never make it cited or deferred -- F2 scaffolds it and F2.5-F4 attempt and review it. Build-inline pieces, all with existing analogues: the perfect-matching representation and its conditional-covariance concentration are [def:perfect-matching-handle] (Doob edge-revelation, analogous to `EdgeVarianceBound.var_edge_sum_le`); the one-at-a-time Lindeberg replacement (11)-(12) matches the first two moments of a Rademacher and a standard normal and needs only a bounded third derivative; the Gaussian covariance interpolation (13)-(15) is Gaussian integration by parts regularized by C(t) + delta I and dominated convergence as delta -> 0, which is exactly what keeps the argument valid on singular ranges; the quadratic comparison is a smooth cutoff at L = G^{1/8} plus the fourth-moment truncation supplied by lem:block-moments and the PSD-square-root fourth-moment identity for the Gaussian side. Search trace: `npm run search -- "Lindeberg replacement smooth test function Gaussian interpolation covariance"`, `npm run search -- "finite population Gaussian approximation permutation statistic"`, `lean_local_search stein_cdf_clt / SteinMethod / var_edge_sum_le / posSqrt`, Mathlib-side `lean_leansearch "Lindeberg replacement trick Gaussian interpolation"` and `lean_loogle "ProbabilityTheory.charFun"`. Result: neither library has a weighted (soft-tilted) quadratic-moment transport, and Causalean's Stein machinery gives Kolmogorov-distance CLT bounds rather than weighted second-moment comparison -- but every INGREDIENT above is present or elementary, so this is build-inline work, not missing substrate.
